title: Bins before Breakfast
story: The bin lorry usually passed before Omar left for work, yet this week the street was still full when he opened the door. He dragged the containers to the pavement and warned his housemate that a late collection meant an earlier start. They agreed to set a shared alarm on collection day. By Friday the pavement was clear before either of them had finished breakfast.

vocabulary.definition: On most occasions, rather than every single time.
Large bins used for holding rubbish.
The path for people along the side of a street.
A person who lives in the same home.
The scheduled pickup of the bins.
Empty of the things that were there before.

quiz.question: What did Omar do with the containers?
options: He dragged them out to the pavement
He left them inside the kitchen
He loaded them onto the lorry himself
He hid them behind the house
quiz.correctAnswer: He dragged them out to the pavement
quiz.explanation: Omar dragged the containers to the pavement before warning his housemate.
quiz.supportingSentence: He dragged the containers to the pavement and warned his housemate that a late collection meant an earlier start.

quiz.question: Why was the street still full when Omar opened the door?
options: The bins had not been collected at the usual time
His housemate had filled the road with boxes
Omar had forgotten to close the front door
The new alarm had woken the whole street
quiz.correctAnswer: The bins had not been collected at the usual time
quiz.explanation: The lorry normally passed before he left, so a full street means the pickup had not happened yet.
quiz.supportingSentence: The bin lorry usually passed before Omar left for work, yet this week the street was still full when he opened the door.

quiz.question: What does the clear pavement on Friday suggest?
options: The containers had gone out early enough to be collected
The lorry had stopped visiting their street
They had cancelled the shared alarm
Breakfast was being served outside
quiz.correctAnswer: The containers had gone out early enough to be collected
quiz.explanation: The pavement was clear before breakfast, which shows the bins were no longer waiting in the street.
quiz.supportingSentence: By Friday the pavement was clear before either of them had finished breakfast.

quiz.question: What does collection mean in this story?
options: The scheduled pickup of the bins
A meeting of every housemate
A box kept for breakfast
A day off from work
quiz.correctAnswer: The scheduled pickup of the bins
quiz.explanation: A late collection is the reason they would need to start earlier with the bins.
quiz.supportingSentence: He dragged the containers to the pavement and warned his housemate that a late collection meant an earlier start.

quiz.question: Why did they decide to set a shared alarm?
options: So they would be up in time on collection day
So the lorry would arrive later in the week
So Omar could stay at home on Friday
So the containers could remain indoors
quiz.correctAnswer: So they would be up in time on collection day
quiz.explanation: A late pickup meant an earlier start, so the alarm was meant to get them up for it.
quiz.supportingSentence: He dragged the containers to the pavement and warned his housemate that a late collection meant an earlier start.
